candidateEvaluations.label: Capture the affine chain in a CUDA graph and replay it as a single launch
candidateEvaluations.title: Capture the affine chain in a CUDA graph and replay it as a single launch
candidateEvaluations.hypothesis: With a 3-kernel eager chain measured at ~11.1us p50 on 32x256, collapse the launch gaps by capturing addcmul/add_/clamp_min_ once on the caller's (stable) input buffers into a CUDA graph; steady-state calls then cost one graph launch instead of three kernel launches, with the same total GPU work.
candidateEvaluations.change: run.py only. Adds: a per-(device,dtype) cached 0-dim constant pair; _affine() doing torch.addcmul(bias, x, scale_x) -> acc.add_(y, alpha=0.75) -> acc.clamp_min_(0.0); _capture_entry() that warms up on a side stream, captures torch.cuda.CUDAGraph, validates the replay against eager with allclose(rtol=atol=1e-5), and keeps the graph only if a 10-iteration event timing shows replay is faster than eager; _graph_output() that captures lazily only when the identical (data_ptr, shape, stride, storage_offset, dtype, device) buffer key is observed twice, so per-call-fresh inputs never trigger repeated captures; a global capture budget of 4 and a permanent disable-on-exception path; run() falls back to _affine() or _affine_generic(). No input is mutated, no result is cached, and every call recomputes from the current contents of inputs.
